key_insight: YOR is an open-source, low-cost mobile manipulator whose combination of an omnidirectional base and telescopic lift yields a compact, affordable platform that supports generalizable robot-learning research. It provides a standardized, modular hardware+software stack so researchers can train and evaluate manipulation policies on realistic mobile platforms.
problem_solved: Lack of an affordable, reproducible mobile manipulation form factor that balances mobility, vertical reach, and ease-of-use for robot-learning experiments and benchmarking.
method: Hardware design that pairs an omnidirectional base with a telescopic vertical lift and modular manipulation components to maximize reach, maneuverability, and cost-effectiveness.
Open-source software stack and interfaces that enable standardized data collection, control, and training of policies for transferable mobile manipulation tasks.
Design-for-reproducibility: modular BOM, assembly guides, and benchmarking protocols to lower the barrier for labs and hobbyists to reproduce and compare results.
impact: YOR democratizes mobile manipulation research by lowering cost and replication friction, enabling broader experimentation on generalization and real-world robot learning. Practitioners can benchmark algorithms on a shared physical platform and accelerate progress toward robust, deployable manipulation systems.
